purpose: the LoRA fine-tune's train corpus for family G-D, derived BY EXCLUSION from the falsifier's eval half so the frozen comparison set stays frozen

geometry.note: limit_natural is the LAUNCHER's 1200, not the parser's 2000 default

disjointness.method: set intersection on window SEQUENCE content, not on indices
disjointness.why: a LoRA run that touched an eval window would look like a WIN, because a generator reproduces what it memorised

honest_limits: This is a SPLIT, not a fine-tune. No model was loaded and no training was run.

Disjointness is proven for the CONTENT of these windows. Two distinct genomic loci with identical 150 bp sequence would collapse to one key -- that is the conservative direction (it can only move a window OUT of train), but it means the train count is a lower bound rather than an exact partition.
The bar it serves (below 0.6679, mode `both`) is the falsifier's, unchanged.
